```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(rungekutta)
library(ggplot2)
```

## A simple equation: y' = y

```{r exp}
f <- function(t, y) y
e <- euler(f, y0 = 1, t0 = 0, tf = 2, h = 0.2)
r <- rk4(f,   y0 = 1, t0 = 0, tf = 2, h = 0.2)
exact <- data.frame(t = e$t, y1 = exp(e$t))

comparer_solutions(Exact = exact, Euler = e, RK4 = r)
```

## Order of convergence

The global error is O(h) for Euler and O(h^4) for RK4.

```{r convergence}
steps <- c(0.5, 0.25, 0.1, 0.05, 0.025)
error <- function(method, h) {
  sol <- method(f, y0 = 1, t0 = 0, tf = 2, h = h)
  abs(tail(sol$y1, 1) - exp(2))
}
err <- data.frame(
  h      = rep(steps, 2),
  method = rep(c("Euler", "RK4"), each = length(steps)),
  error  = c(sapply(steps, function(h) error(euler, h)),
             sapply(steps, function(h) error(rk4,   h)))
)

ggplot(err, aes(h, error, colour = method)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  labs(colour = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

# Log-log slopes: they estimate the order of each method
sapply(c("Euler", "RK4"), function(m) {
  d <- err[err$method == m, ]
  unname(coef(lm(log(error) ~ log(h), data = d))[2])
})
```

## An epidemic: the SIR model

```{r sir}
sir <- rk4(modele_sir(beta = 0.3, gamma = 0.1, N = 1000),
           y0 = c(S = 999, I = 1, R = 0), t0 = 0, tf = 160, h = 0.5)
plot(sir)
sir[which.max(sir$I), ]   # epidemic peak
```
